question.text: Under the general rule of the SEBI (FPI) Regulations, 2019, what is the aggregate contribution limit of NRIs, OCIs, and Resident Indian individuals in the corpus of an FPI applicant?

answer.text: Below 40 percent of the total contribution in the corpus
Below 75 percent of the total contribution in the corpus
Below 25 percent of the total contribution in the corpus
Below 50 percent of the total contribution in the corpus

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the general rule in the SEBI (FPI) Regulations, 2019, the aggregate contribution of NRIs, OCIs, and Resident Indian individuals in the corpus of an FPI applicant shall be below 50 percent of the total contribution in the corpus. The 2026 III-C workbook also notes exceptions where this clause is not applicable, including specified IFSC-regulated applicants and SWAGAT-FI, but the general-rule cap remains below 50 percent. The Trap: The single individual contribution limit is below 25 percent, while the aggregate limit for NRIs, OCIs and Resident Indian individuals taken together is below 50 percent. Candidates often swap these two numbers. The 40 percent and 75 percent options are distractor figures with no basis in the regulation. Note: Keep the two numbers separate: the single-individual cap is below 25 percent, while the aggregate cap for NRIs, OCIs, and Resident Indians combined is below 50 percent.
